## GET /admin-api/caep

`getCaep`

**The CAEP session register: what state each session is in and how many events of which type have been sent about it**

Everything /admin/caep and /admin/caep-sessions draw, as JSON. Per session: who it belongs to, when it was established, the CAEP state it is in — established, presented, revoked — its assurance level, its device compliance, its risk level, the claims that have changed, and a count per event type.

THE REGISTER OUTLIVES THE SESSION AND THAT IS THE POINT. The session store forgets one the moment it is signed out, so a row saying `revoked` is the only remaining evidence that it existed and was revoked.

CAEP IS A VOCABULARY AND NOT A FAMILY. Its events travel on SSF streams, are signed by the SSF signer and are delivered by the two SSF deliveries, so GET /admin-api/ssf is where the streams themselves are. `streams` here says only which of them would take a CAEP event at all, because a session with a count of zero almost always means nobody asked for that type — and SSF gives a receiver no other notice of that.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/caep` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**200**: The register, the catalogue and the settings.

## POST /admin-api/caep/clear

`clearCaepSessions`

**Drop every row in the CAEP session register**

Forgets what has been said about every session. Nobody is signed out, no stream is touched and no queued event is dropped — those are the SSF half, at POST /admin-api/ssf/delete.

It is worth knowing what this throws away: rows for sessions this service NO LONGER HOLDS are the only evidence that those sessions existed and were revoked, and nothing else in this service records it.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/caep` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body** (optional)

An empty object.

**200**: How many rows were dropped.

|---|---|---|---|
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |

**400**: The operation was refused; `errors` says why and nothing changed.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |

## POST /admin-api/caep/emit

`emitCaepEvent`

**Send one CAEP event about one session**

Builds the payload, adds the four claims CAEP gives every event, composes the SUBJECT from the session — SSF's complex subject, naming the person AND the session, because the person is not revoked and one session of theirs is — and transmits it on every stream that both delivers the type and covers that subject.

EVERY ONE OF THE EIGHT ALSO FIRES ON ITS OWN when `caep.autoEmit` is on — `device-compliance-change` since #164, from the device register — so this is for an event on demand, about a session and with a payload you chose.

A TYPE NO STREAM TAKES IS NOT AN ERROR. The session's state is still updated and the reply says nothing was sent, because "the event happened and nobody had asked to hear about it" is a different fact from a failure and is the one that is usually true.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/caep` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `initiating_entity` | one of `admin`, `user`, `policy`, `system` |  | admin \| user \| policy \| system. It is the member that lets a receiver tell "an administrator revoked this" from "a risk engine did". |
| `payload` | string |  | The event-specific members, as JSON. Empty for a conforming specimen of the type. |
| `reason_admin` | string |  | Why, for a log. Sent as an object keyed by `caep.reasonLanguage` — CAEP makes it a language map and a string there is the commonest mistake in the profile. |
| `reason_user` | string |  | The same, in words meant for the person. |
| `session_id` | string | yes | The session it is about, from GET /admin-api/caep. |
| `type` | string | yes | The event type: a short name such as `session-revoked`, or the whole URI. |

**200**: How many streams took it, or why none did.

|---|---|---|---|

| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |
| `reports` | list |  |  |
| `reports[].claims` | any JSON |  | A Security Event Token's claims. ## POST /admin-api/caep/reset-session

`resetCaepSession`

**Put one session's CAEP state back to where it started**

Clears the state, the assurance level, the device compliance, the risk level, the changed claims and every counter on one row, keeping the row.

IT SIGNS NOBODY OUT. This register is a record of what has been SAID about a session; resetting it forgets the record. The session itself is untouched and every token issued on it is still good, which is the distinction this whole page rests on.

It is a reset and not a delete because the identity and the sign-in instant are still true — a delete would take the row off the page, which reads as the session having gone.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/caep` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `session_id` | string | yes | The session. |

|---|---|---|---|
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |

**400**: The operation was refused; `errors` says why and nothing changed.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `errors` | list |  |  |

| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |

## GET /admin-api/caep/sessions

`getCaepSessions`

**The CAEP session register, searched and paged — or one session with everything that has been said about it**

What /admin/caep-sessions draws. Without `session` it is the register: one row per session this service has HELD, including the ones it no longer holds, with its CAEP state, assurance, device compliance, risk and a count per event type — searched with `sessq` and paged with `sessionsPage` and `per`. Beside it, `applications`: what this transmitter has said to each RECEIVER across every session, searched with `appq` and paged with `applicationsPage`. That is the third question this page answers and the one somebody arrives with once more than one receiver exists — the sessions are per SESSION, the streams are per STREAM, and this is per APPLICATION.

With `session` it is that one session opened out: the events actually sent about it, in order, with the jti and the stream each went out on and what the register noticed as it was applied, paged with `eventsPage`.

**THE REGISTER OUTLIVES THE SESSION AND THAT IS THE POINT.** The session store forgets one the moment it is signed out, so a row saying `revoked` is the only remaining evidence that it existed and was revoked — and it is why this is not the same list as GET /admin-api/sessions, which is what is LIVE.

A `session` that names nothing answers 200 with `session: null` rather than 404: this register is capped at `caep.maxSessionsTracked` and drops the oldest, so an old identifier coming back empty is an ordinary outcome and not a missing resource.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/caep-sessions` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sessq` | query | string |  | Narrows the register to rows whose username, `sub`, session id, SSF subject or protocol contains this. |
| `session` | query | string |  | One session id. The reply is then that session and its events rather than the list. |
| `sessionsPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of the register. Clamped, like every page parameter here. |
| `appq` | query | string |  | Narrows the per-receiver list to rows whose application name, identifier or stream `aud` contains this. It deliberately does NOT match event types: a receiver that takes none of the eight is exactly the row somebody is looking for when they ask why nothing arrived. |
| `applicationsPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of the per-receiver list. It shares `per` with the register above it, which is the arrangement every page here that carries two lists has. |
| `streamsPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of the streams a CAEP event could go to. It shares `per` with the two lists above. |
| `eventsPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of ONE session's events, with `session`. |
| `page` | query | integer |  | Which page of the match to return. CLAMPED rather than refused: a page past the end returns the last one, and the reply says which page it actually is. |
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 300. On a drill-down it is SHARED by every list in the reply, which each carry a page number of their own. |

**200**: The register, or one session and its events.
